links.outcome: Accuracy of a published MALDI-MS/ML pipeline applied unchanged to local Kazakhstan samples
links.effect: Applied as is, SARS-CoV-2+ detection was 91.0%, but accuracy was low for NCARI (48.0%) and AC (67.0%) with the top random forest model.
links.quote: Applying the established MALDI-MS pipeline ”as is” resulted in a high detection rate for SARS-CoV-2+ samples (91.0%), but low accuracy for NCARI (48.0%) and AC (67.0%) by the top-performing random forest model.

links.outcome: Local accuracy after retraining ML models on combined South American and Kazakhstan data
links.effect: After retraining, SVM-RBF accuracy was 88.0%, 95.0% and 78% for Kazakhstan SARS-CoV-2+, NCARI and AC; SARS-CoV-2 vs. rest ROC AUC 0.983 [0.958, 0.987].
links.quote: After re-training of the ML algorithms on the SA-Kaz peak intensity matrix, the accuracy of detection by the top-performing Support Vector Machine with radial basis function kernel model was at 88.0, 95.0 and 78% for the Kazakhstan SARS-CoV-2+, NCARI, and AC subjects, respectively with a SARS-CoV-2 vs. rest ROC AUC of 0.983 [0.958, 0.987]; a high differentiation accuracy was maintained for the South American SARS-CoV-2 and NCARI.
